LABEL: Phase 2A ABORTED at task 23/30 - granite4.1:3b, harness_version 2, 2026-09-03
status: ABORTED. Partial results are NOT a measurement and are not reported as one.
abort_rule: pre-authorised: more than 5 tasks flagged memory-suspect -> abort mid-run, do not salvage

WHY_THIS_ABORT_MATTERS.headline: The abort condition did its job, and it caught a real defect rather than a noisy threshold.
WHY_THIS_ABORT_MATTERS.what_I_got_wrong: Mid-run I judged the commit-ratio flags to be false positives - 'too tight by roughly 0.05', 'three of these five are false positives' - because the flagged tasks were not slow. That was WRONG. The flags were tracking a monotonic leak, and the flagged tasks were not slow YET.
WHY_THIS_ABORT_MATTERS.what_stopped_the_mistake: Refusing to retune a threshold mid-run because loosening it would conveniently avoid an abort. The rule held; the analysis that would have overridden it was the thing that was wrong.

THE_FINDING_fifth_process_class_bug.name: the model worker leaks across a long run, and the leak is invisible in free memory
THE_FINDING_fifth_process_class_bug.class: process - FIFTH. The first three were 'anything spawned outlives what spawned it'; the fourth was 'the reaper cannot tell a live child from an orphan'; this one is 'a live, legitimate worker grows without bound'.

evidence_monotonic.why_this_is_the_smoking_gun: 23 consecutive readings with not one decrease. Pressure from other applications fluctuates; this only ever climbs. Free memory over the same span oscillated 0.44 -> 2.34 -> 1.41, so free memory alone CANNOT see this.

evidence_isolation.harness_process_is_innocent: commit ratio was 1.431 AFTER the python harness was killed - higher than the 1.421 recorded while it ran. The growth is not in the measurement process.
evidence_isolation.model_commitment_growth_gb: 3.48 -> 6.68, i.e. +3.20 GB over 23 tasks = ~139 MB per task

CONSEQUENCES: WALL-CLOCK IS CONFOUNDED WITH POSITION IN THE RUN. Suite order is fixed (E01-E10, M11-M22, H23-H30), so tasks that run late are measured under progressively worse memory conditions than tasks that run early. Hard tasks run LAST.

That means 'hard tasks are slower' is partly 'hard tasks run last'. In this partial run hard-tier median wall is 442.2s against easy 132.9s, and the hard tasks were also the ones at the highest commit ratios. The two explanations are not separated by this design.
budget_exhausted is a TIME limit, so the leak makes it progressively more likely later in a run - manufacturing apparent difficulty that is really lateness.
It scales with run LENGTH, so it hits the longest runs hardest: the paired calibration (2 arms x 30 tasks) and M11 are far more exposed than this 30-task pass.
Extrapolated: ~139 MB/task means a 60-arm paired run adds ~8 GB of commitment on a 15.47 GB machine.
PROPOSED_FIX: Refresh the worker on a schedule or on a commit-ratio trigger during long runs (unload + reload reclaims it fully), and RECORD which tasks paid a reload so the cold-load cost stays visible rather than smearing into the task's time.

Randomise or rotate task order per run so position stops being confounded with tier. This changes no pass criterion, so it does not bump HARNESS_VERSION, but it does change wall-clock comparability and must be stated.
Record llama-server RSS per task alongside the commit ratio, so the leak is visible in the data instead of inferred from it.

PARTIAL_DATA_NOT_A_MEASUREMENT.WHY_NOT_REPORTED_AS_A_RESULT: The abort rule says partial results are not salvaged as a measurement, and independently the leak means later tasks were measured under different conditions from earlier ones. A mean over 23 tasks measured on a drifting instrument is not a pass rate. These numbers are recorded to document the abort, not to be quoted.
PARTIAL_DATA_NOT_A_MEASUREMENT.resumable: runs/phase2a-3b-30tasks.json.partial.jsonl holds all 23 with an fsync per task, so a corrected re-run resumes rather than repeats - but it SHOULD NOT resume until the leak is addressed, because resuming would blend pre-fix and post-fix conditions.

ONE_RESULT_THAT_SURVIVES.claim: R1 answer position predicts full-loop outcome
ONE_RESULT_THAT_SURVIVES.evidence: 4 for 4 on the tasks where both measurements exist: E01 collapsed at R1 -> failed the loop; E03 did not collapse -> passed; E04 collapsed -> failed; E05 partial with majority answer-last -> passed.
ONE_RESULT_THAT_SURVIVES.why_it_survives_the_abort: It is a per-task correspondence between two independent measurements, not an aggregate over the run, so the drifting instrument does not touch it. Pass/fail is decided by the grader on the artifact; the leak corrupts SECONDS, not verification.
ONE_RESULT_THAT_SURVIVES.caveat: n=4, all easy tier, single samples in the loop arm. Suggestive, not established.

preflight_check_inconsistency.observed: noise.py's preflight printed 'under 2 GB free even after reaping' and warned, because the model was deliberately kept warm (1.2 GB free is the healthy resident state).
preflight_check_inconsistency.cause: the 2 GB free-memory rule still exists in noise.py's PREFLIGHT while the per-task check was moved to commit ratio. The same wrong comparison - a model-resident reading against a no-model rule - survives in the place that was not fixed.
preflight_check_inconsistency.severity: warns only, does not abort, so it did not affect this run
preflight_check_inconsistency.action: fix the preflight to use memory_pressure() too, so one rule is not expressed two incompatible ways
